description: Secondary inspection, additional questioning and device searches rise and fall with the news cycle, which means the person's experience of a border is set by events they have no connection to.
energy_note: Your airport experience is set by a newspaper.

aspect: It reaches children at school immediately
description: Playground abuse follows broadcast news within days. The child has no context for it, has often never seen the country, and comes home with a question the parents have no good answer to.
energy_note: Explaining a war to a nine-year-old who was called a name.

aspect: Employment effects are real and deniable
description: Security clearance exclusions, export-control restrictions, and hiring hesitancy that never states its reason. Each individual decision is defensible and the aggregate is a wall.
energy_note: Never rejected for it. Never hired either.
notes: Overlaps assets/text/iran; kept here because wartime spikes are a distinct phenomenon from the baseline.

aspect: The stereotype is inherited by people who never lived there
description: Second and third generation descendants hold a name, a face and no connection, and receive the treatment anyway. Transmission here is entirely social - nothing biological is required.
energy_note: Inheriting a reputation you never earned.
